# Local patches on top of vendored Bluedroid

`third_party/bluedroid/` is upstream ESP-IDF `ad20ded62a2d67a26e501fdc1905f43ba7ad6c81`
(`components/bt/host/bluedroid`, `components/bt/common`, `components/esp_ringbuf`, one header from
`components/bt/ble_profiles/common`). The first commit that added it is byte-identical to upstream; every
local change is a separate commit **and** a `.patch` file here, so an upgrade is: re-vendor, re-apply, rebuild.

| Patch | File | Why |
|---|---|---|
| 0001 | `host/bluedroid/common/include/common/bt_target.h` | Upstream hard-codes `BTA/BTC_AV_SINK_INCLUDED=TRUE` whenever A2DP is on. `OPENFW_A2DP_SOURCE_ONLY` (set in `bt_port/bt_port_prefix.h`) drops the sink and SBC decoder: -9.6 KB RAM (`a2dp_sink_local_param`), ~-10 KB flash. |
| 0002 | `host/bluedroid/btc/profile/std/a2dp/btc_a2dp_source.c` | `BTC_MEDIA_AA_BUF_SIZE` (4112) is allocated per encoded frame (up to 5 queued) although frames are <= the 1008 B A2DP MTU. Make it overridable (we use 1280): -14 KB peak heap. |
| 0003 | `host/bluedroid/bta/av/bta_av_api.c` | `BTA_GetDelayValue()` is built unconditionally but its event exists only with the sink: upstream does not compile source-only. |
| 0004 | `host/bluedroid/device/controller.c` | Host Buffer Size (`0C33`) announces `L2CAP_MTU_SIZE` (1691 B) as the host ACL length. Make it overridable (`L2CAP_HOST_FC_ACL_DATA_LEN`, we use 1021 = controller ACL length) so the controller->host window (4 x 1021 B, plan M1) fits bt_ctrl's RX ring; L2CAP reassembly MTU unchanged. |
| 0005 | `common/osi/alarm.c`, `osi/include/osi/alarm.h` | The esp_timer shim (`bt_port/bt_esp_timer.c` on `bt_alarm`) delivers expiries in BTC context after generation validation, so `alarm_cb_handler` calls the callback directly instead of `btc_transfer_context` (which allocates and can block). Adds `osi_alarm_generation()` / `osi_alarm_delivery_gen()` for re-validation under a caller's lock (plan M2 "Alarms"). |
| 0006 | `common/btc/core/btc_task.c` | Drain pending alarms after every BTC message, and `btc_post_alarm_drain()`: allocation-free, timeout-0 post of a drain work item. A failed post implies a full queue, so the drain-after-every-message guarantees delivery. |
| 0007 | `host/bluedroid/hci/hci_layer.c` | `command_timed_out` ignores an expiry whose generation no longer matches the command-response timer (checked under `commands_pending_response_lock`, where the timer is armed/cancelled), and reports surviving timeouts to `bt_port_on_hci_command_timeout()` (BT fault path). |
| 0008 | `host/bluedroid/hci/hci_hal_h4.c` | `host_recv_pkt_cb()` (the driver's `notify_host_recv`) asserts when the RX copy cannot be allocated and ignores `fixed_queue_enqueue()`'s result (leaked copy, lost packet: a lost CC stalls command dispatch). Both now return `-1` to the driver, which keeps its copy and retries (`docs/BT_HCI_DRIVER_CONTRACT.md` §13.1, plan M1 "No silent loss in host RX"). |
| 0009 | `common/osi/fixed_queue.c` | `fixed_queue_enqueue()` gives the slot back (`enqueue_sem`) when `list_append()` fails, so a failed node allocation no longer shrinks the queue permanently (contract §13.2). |
| 0010 | `host/bluedroid/hci/hci_layer.c` | NOACK commands (`0C35` Host Number Of Completed Packets) get their own queue, drained by hciT ahead of the command-credit check, of credit-blocked commands and of a pending ACL fragment, so the C2H credit return can always leave the host (contract §13.3, plan M1 credit window). |

| 0011 | `host/bluedroid/hci/hci_packet_factory.c` | `make_command()` asserts when the command buffer cannot be allocated. It returns NULL and every builder that writes parameters returns that NULL before touching the stream (`OPENFW_RETURN_IF_NO_PACKET`). |
| 0012 | `host/bluedroid/device/controller.c`, `host/bluedroid/hci/hci_layer.c` | Controller start-up (`start_up()`, run from `BTM_DeviceReset()` on the BTU task) aborts on the first command that cannot be built (0011) or queued: `transmit_command_futured()` frees the command and returns NULL when `future_new()` fails (upstream asserts / dereferences NULL). The controller stays not ready (`readable == false`). |
| 0013 | `host/bluedroid/stack/btm/btm_devctl.c`, `host/bluedroid/bta/dm/bta_dm_act.c` | A failed enable is reported, not asserted or left hanging: `BTM_DeviceReset()` reports `BTM_DEV_STATUS_DOWN` when start-up failed; BTA DM tracks a pending enable and turns that hardware error, or a failed `BTA_SYS_API_ENABLE` allocation (upstream `assert(0)`), into `BTA_DM_ENABLE_EVT` with `BTA_FAILURE` after undoing `bta_dm_enable()` -> `esp_bluedroid_enable()` returns `ESP_FAIL`. |
| 0014 | `host/bluedroid/bta/sys/bta_sys_main.c`, `bta/include/bta/bta_sys.h`, `bta/dm/bta_dm_act.c` | BTA SYS events posted from the BTU task to itself (`EVT_ENABLED`, `STACK_ENABLED`/`ERROR` from BTM, `EVT_DISABLED`, DM's `API_DISABLE` from the disable timer) are silently dropped upstream when the message cannot be allocated (enable/disable never complete). They now run synchronously from a stack copy through the same state table (`bta_sys_hw_execute_local()`). |
| 0015 | `host/bluedroid/hci/hci_layer.c` | Commands awaiting CC/CS are linked through their own `pkt_linked_item_t` (STAILQ) instead of a `list_t` node allocated after the command was dequeued; upstream sent the command even when that node allocation failed, so its reply matched nothing (futured start-up command: BTU blocked forever; callback command: leak, completion never runs). Deinit frees commands still pending. |
| 0016 | `host/bluedroid/stack/btu/btu_hcif.c` | CC/CS hand-off from hciT to BTU: upstream dereferences an unchecked `osi_calloc()` (and leaks the response/command if the post fails). Bounded retry (`OPENFW_HCIF_HANDOFF_RETRIES` = 8, 1 tick apart, same policy as `bt_dlv`); if memory does not come back the event is dropped, its buffers freed and the loss reported through the 0007 hook (BT fault -> recovery ladder). |
| 0017 | `host/bluedroid/btc/core/btc_dm.c` | `btc_dm_sec_cb_handler()` allocated the BLE GAP message for every DM security event and returned on failure, losing `BTA_DM_ENABLE_EVT`/`DISABLE_EVT`. The handler now fills a header on the stack and allocates the full message only for events forwarded to BLE GAP. |
| 0018 | `host/bluedroid/btc/core/btc_dm.c` | When the BTA -> BTC hand-off (`btc_transfer_context`, allocates) of `BTA_DM_ENABLE_EVT`/`DISABLE_EVT` fails, the event (at most a status) is posted by value (`osi_thread_post`, no allocation) to BTC queue 0, which runs the same handler from a stack message: enable/disable complete instead of hanging. |
| 0019 | `host/bluedroid/bta/sys/bta_sys_main.c` | `bta_sys_start_timer()` allocates the alarm and a hash-map entry on a timer's first start and silently gives up on failure (BTA DM's disable timer: disable hangs). Bounded retry (`OPENFW_BTA_TIMER_RETRIES` = 8, 1 tick apart, outside `bta_alarm_lock`). |
| 0020 | `common/osi/fixed_queue.c` | `fixed_queue_new()` treats a failed `osi_mutex_new()` like its other members (returns NULL) instead of asserting. |
| 0021 | `host/bluedroid/hci/hci_hal_h4.c`, `host/bluedroid/hci/hci_layer.c` | HCI init: `hci_hal_env_init()` / `hci_layer_init_env()` return failure instead of asserting on the RX queue and the up/downstream events, and check the pending-response mutex (upstream ignored it: NULL-mutex lock on the first command). `hci_start_up()` cleans up, `esp_bluedroid_init()` fails. |
| 0022 | `stack/btu/btu_init.c`, `btu_task.c`, `stack/include/stack/btu.h`, `stack/btm/btm_main.c`, `btm_dev.c`, `stack/l2cap/l2c_main.c`, `bta/sys/bta_sys_main.c`, `bta/include/bta/bta_sys.h` | BTU start-up: the three alarm mutexes are checked; `btu_init_core()`'s component inits (asserts removed in `btm_init`/`btm_sec_dev_init`; `l2c_init`/`sdp_init`/`btm_acl_init` ignored failures upstream) and `bta_sys_init()` are verified (`btu_init_core_ok()`, `bta_sys_init_ok()`), a failure completes the init with `BT_STATUS_NOMEM`; `btu_task_shut_down()` frees the core only if `btu_task_start_up()` ran (upstream freed never-initialised control blocks after a failed `BTU_StartUp()`: `l2c_free()` asserted on a NULL list), and `l2c_free()` tolerates NULL pools. |
| 0023 | `common/osi/alarm.c`, `host/bluedroid/btc/core/btc_main.c`, `common/osal/src/bt_osal_freertos.c` | BTC init: `osi_alarm_create_mux()` reports a failed mutex (upstream: assert in `osi_alarm_init()`); `btc_config_init()`'s result is checked and it runs BEFORE `bte_main_boot_entry()` (after it, BTU may already have completed the init future, so a later failure could not be reported); the bt_osal function table is used in place instead of a heap copy whose allocation failure asserted after an otherwise successful init. |
| 0024 | `host/bluedroid/btc/profile/std/spp/btc_spp.c` | `bta_jv_act.c` passes `RFCOMM_START`, `RFCOMM_CL_INIT`, `RFCOMM_WRITE`, `FREE_SCN`, `DISABLE` and `DISCOVERY_COMP` as a pointer to the event's own (smaller) struct cast to `tBTA_JV *`; `btc_spp_rfcomm_inter_cb()` / `btc_spp_dm_inter_cb()` copied `sizeof(tBTA_JV)` from it into the BTC message: a stack over-read on every `esp_spp_write()`. They copy the event's member size (`btc_spp_jv_evt_len()`). Found by ASan, `test_bt_host phone`. |
| 0025 | `host/bluedroid/bta/dm/bta_dm_act.c` | The `BD_NAME` BTM's security callbacks (and `BTM_SecReadDevName()`) hand BTA is the device record's 65-byte `sec_bd_name`; three sites `memcpy`'d 247 bytes from it (heap over-read on every bond). `BTA_DM_COPY_BTM_NAME()` copies `BTM_MAX_REM_BD_NAME_LEN` and terminates. Found by ASan, `test_bt_host phone`. |
| 0026 | `host/bluedroid/bta/dm/bta_dm_act.c` | `bta_dm_disable()` with ACL links up waited 5 s for profiles to close them, then detached and waited 1.5 s more: the link-down that would end the wait never arrives because `bta_sys_disable()` has already deregistered BTA DM itself. Every disable with a phone connected took 6.5 s, past the plan's 2 s teardown deadline (hard path + reboot on each BT-mode exit). Detach after `OPENFW_BTA_DM_DISABLE_LINK_WAIT_MS` (100) and report after `OPENFW_BTA_DM_DISABLE_DETACH_WAIT_MS` (500): ~0.63 s with a connected SPP peer and data outstanding (`test_bt_host phone`, step P8; reverted: 5.0 s with a responsive peer, 6.7 s with a stalled one). |
| 0027 | `host/bluedroid/stack/btu/btu_task.c` | `BTU_ShutDown()` frees `btu_thread` before `btu_task_shut_down()` -> `btu_free_core()` -> `l2c_free()` releases the link control blocks. A link whose Disconnection Complete never came (phone out of range: 0026 reports DISABLE ~600 ms after its detach either way, then `bt_ctrl` stops the controller) goes through `l2cu_release_lcb()` -> `btm_acl_removed()` -> `bta_sys_sendmsg()` -> `btu_task_post()` -> `osi_thread_post(NULL)`: assert, or a NULL dereference without asserts, in the BTC task during `esp_bluedroid_deinit()`. `btu_task_post()` now fails when the thread is gone; every caller already handles a failed post (`bta_sys_sendmsg` frees the message, its upstream comment expects this race). Found in review; `test_bt_host phone` step P12 (fake ROM `defer_detach`) crashed without it. |
| 0028 | `host/bluedroid/bta/dm/bta_dm_act.c` | `bta_dm_sp_cback()` reports a User Confirmation Request whose peer name is unknown from `bta_dm_pinname_cback()` after a remote name request, with `bta_dm_cb.num_val`; upstream stores that value only after the name branch (which returns first), so the user was shown the previous pairing's value or 0. The value is stored before the name branch. Found on silicon (bench 2026-11-24: "value 0" logged while the laptop showed 230749); `test_bt_host phone` step P17 (first name request fails, `fake_peer.name_fail_n`) failed without it (logged the previous pairing's 123634, want 123668). |
| 0029 | `common/osi/alarm.c` | `alarm_cb_handler()` read `alarm->cb` and `alarm->cb_data` without `alarm_mutex` or generation re-validation after `bt_alarm_drain()` left its critical section; a higher-priority task (e.g. BTU) preempting there with `osi_alarm_free()` (+ `osi_alarm_new()`) raced on `alarm_cbs[]` and could invoke an unarmed new alarm's callback or `cb(NULL)`. Revalidate `alarm_state`, `alarm_hdl` and `osi_alarm_delivery_gen() == osi_alarm_generation(alarm)` and snapshot `(cb, cb_data)` under `alarm_mutex`. Review r1 (R1-03); `test_bt_host patch29` (drain-exit hook: free + new from a higher-priority task) failed without it. |
| 0030 | `common/osi/thread.c`, `osi/include/osi/thread.h`, `host/bluedroid/hci/hci_layer.c`, `stack/btu/btu_hcif.c` | `hci_shut_down()` destroyed `rx_q` (`hal->close()`) and `commands_pending_response_lock` / `command_queue` (`hci_layer_deinit_env()`) before `osi_thread_free(hci_host_thread)`; if `hci_host_thread` was sleeping in 0016's hand-off OOM retry or preempted mid-packet, it resumed into freed queues/mutexes (`configASSERT` / UAF). Export idempotent `osi_thread_stop()` + `osi_thread_is_stopping()`, stop `hci_host_thread` before tearing down HAL/HCI env, and abort 0016's retry loop when stopping. Review r1; `test_bt_host patch30` (0C13 reply held, hand-off OOM during disable/deinit) hit the NULL-mutex `configASSERT` without it. |
| 0031 | `host/bluedroid/bta/sys/bta_sys_main.c` | `bta_sys_free()` left `bta_alarm_hash_map` dangling after `hash_map_free()`. After one clean init+deinit cycle, a second `esp_bluedroid_init()` that fails inside `btu_init_core()` (after 0022 sets `btu_core_started = true`, before `bta_sys_init()` overwrites `bta_alarm_hash_map`) runs `btu_task_shut_down()` -> `bta_sys_free()` -> UAF/double-free in `hash_map_clear()`. Clear `bta_alarm_hash_map = NULL`. Review r1; `test_bt_host patch31` (second cycle with each init allocation failed in turn; `run_sweep.py` cannot see it, one process per point) is a heap-use-after-free under ASan without it. |
| 0032 | `common/osi/config.c` | `config_parse()` allocated exact `buf_size` bytes, passed `CONFIG_FILE_DEFAULE_LENGTH` (2048) instead of remaining buffer capacity to `nvs_get_blob()`, and called `strchr(p_line_bgn, '\n')` without a trailing NUL (heap over-read on an unterminated `/bt_bonds.bin` blob). Also `config_save()` never erased `bt_cfg_key1+` when the config shrank below 1536 B, wasting space in the 4 KiB `bt_store` quota (`BT_STORE_DATA_MAX`). The buffer gets a NUL guard, reads are bounded by the remaining capacity, and stale chunks are erased on save. Review r1; `test_bt_host patch32` is an ASan heap-buffer-overflow (`strchr` in `config_parse`) without it. |
| 0033 | `host/bluedroid/stack/l2cap/l2c_main.c` | `l2c_rcv_acl_data()` read 9 bytes (`handle`, `hci_len`, `l2cap_len`, `rcv_cid`, `cmd_code`) when `l2cu_find_lcb_by_handle()` returned NULL; a 4-byte zero-payload L2CAP frame (`p_msg->len == 8`) passes `packet_fragmenter` and triggers a 1-byte heap over-read at `cmd_code`. Drop frames shorter than 8 B (9 B on unknown handle) through `l2c_rcv_acl_exit` so C2H credit is still returned. Review r1; `test_bt_host patch33` is an ASan heap-buffer-overflow at `cmd_code` without it. |
| 0034 | `host/bluedroid/btc/profile/std/a2dp/btc_a2dp_source_ext_codec.c`, `btc/profile/std/include/btc_a2dp_source.h` | Headphones mode encodes SBC and paces the stream itself through the external-codec source (`CONFIG_BT_A2DP_USE_EXTERNAL_CODEC`, docs/BT_A2DP_DESIGN.md §4-5, "patch A"). `MAX_OUTPUT_A2DP_SRC_FRAME_QUEUE_SZ` (upstream 27) becomes `#ifndef`; `bt_port_prefix.h` sets 3, so `audio_tx_q` holds at most 4 packets (packets wait in our PCM ring, where a seek can still drop them). Queue accounting for the app's position and stall math: cumulative packet and SBC-frame counters (from each buffer's `number_frame`) for enqueue, BTU `readbuf` and tx flushes, read with `btc_a2dp_source_ext_txq_stat()`; `btc_a2dp_source_ext_txq_drop()` (BTC context) frees `audio_tx_q` on a seek or end of file and returns the SBC frames dropped; `btc_a2dp_source_ext_can_send()` lets the tick check "ON and not flushing" before it allocates and pulls PCM (rev 3 §4.3). A failed enqueue (node allocation) is reported to the caller, which keeps its buffer, instead of being ignored. `tests/test_xsrc_stats.c` (`make test-bt-hp`) checks the cap of 4, every counter and the drop's return value. |
| 0035 | `host/bluedroid/external/sbc/encoder/include/sbc_types.h`, `external/sbc/decoder/include/oi_cpu_dep.h` | The SBC codec's 32-bit types are `long` (`SINT32`, and `OI_INT32`/`OI_UINT32` for the hard-wired ARM7 CPU type): 32 bits on Cortex-M4 but 64 on the LP64 host, where the encoder's analysis filter then indexes `s16X` through 64-bit `SINT32` pointers past its buffer (ASan, `test_hp_tx`) and the decoder misparses frames. Both become `int32_t`/`uint32_t`: the same width on target, correct on the host where the SBC round-trip tests run. |
| 0036 | `host/bluedroid/btc/core/btc_dm.c` | Headphones pairing policy (docs/BT_A2DP_DESIGN.md §6.3, "patch D"): `btc_dm_sp_cfm_req_evt()` confirmed Just Works itself (`BTA_DmConfirm(..., true)`) without any app event, so a pairing window, the M2.3 entropy gate and the key-burn rule never applied to headsets. It now asks `openfw_just_works_allowed(bda)` first; the weak default allows everything (phone mode unchanged), `bt_port/bt_hp_bluedroid.c` answers yes only for the picked headset inside its window with the gate holding. `test_bt_host_hp hps` S3 (accepted in the window) and S9 (refused with the window closed). |
| 0037 | `host/bluedroid/btc/profile/std/a2dp/btc_av.c` | `bte_av_callback()` copied `sizeof(tBTA_AV)` from the event pointer, but BTA AV passes each event's own (smaller) struct cast to `tBTA_AV *` (`bta_av_api_enable`: a 2-byte `tBTA_AV_ENABLE` on its stack): a stack over-read on every A2DP event. The event's member size is copied into a zeroed union (`btc_av_evt_len()`), the class of 0024. Found by ASan, `test_bt_host_hp hps` S1. |
| 0038 | `host/bluedroid/bta/av/bta_av_act.c`, `bta_av_aact.c` | Same class in BTA AV: `bta_av_proc_stream_evt()` copied `sizeof(tAVDT_CTRL)` from AVDTP's per-event struct (`avdt_ad_tc_open_ind`: a `tAVDT_OPEN` on its stack), now the event's size (`bta_av_avdt_evt_len()`); `bta_av_dereg_comp()` read `p_data->api_reg.tsep` past both callers' smaller messages (now the local SEP type from the stream block, read before it is freed), and `bta_av_cleanup()` passed it an uninitialised `tBTA_AV_CONN_CHG` whose handle selects the stream block to free (now the stream's own handle). Found by ASan, `test_bt_host_hp hps` S1/S3. |
| 0039 | `host/bluedroid/bta/av/bta_av_main.c` | Teardown with a frozen headset ("patch E", docs/BT_A2DP_DESIGN.md §5.2, lead decision §19.2): A2DP deinit closes the stream and waits for the peer (AVDTP CLOSE up to `BTA_AV_CLOSE_REQ_TIME_VAL` 4 s, L2CAP disconnect up to 10 s); the 2 s teardown then stopped BTU before `BTA_AV_DISABLE_EVT`, and `btc_av` kept its deinit statics for the rest of the boot (the next `esp_a2d_source_init()` failed). `bta_av_api_deregister()` now posts a local AVDT disconnect for a stream left closing, so `BTA_AV_DEREG_COMP`/`DISABLE_EVT` follow at once. `test_bt_host_hp hps` S10: frozen stop 0.64 s (was: deinit timeout, then a second start FAULTED). Known: AVDTP's blocks of the dead link stay allocated (~1.7 KB host, 16 blocks) until reboot. |
| 0040 | `host/bluedroid/stack/btm/btm_acl.c` | `btm_read_remote_ext_features_complete()` read the peer's extended feature pages up to `HCI_EXT_FEATURES_PAGE_MAX` (2). The SL6801 ROM keeps a single 8-byte "remote page 1" slot per link and stores every `LMP_features_res_ext` there whatever its page (ROM `0x21E4C`); its initiator pairing decision (`0x2D85C`, after `040C`) tests bit 0 of that slot (host SSP). Reading page 2 replaced it with page-2 bits (bit 0 = CSB, normally 0), so every pairing the device starts (headphones mode: we page and authenticate as master) fell back to legacy PIN (`0x16`) with SSP peers. Read up to page 1 only; page 2 (Secure Connections, CSB) is unused (`sc_en` false). Silicon 2026-11-25 (bench trace `0411` -> `0x17` -> `040C` -> `0x16`; ROM analysis docs/BT_ROM_HCI_MAP.md §12). Phone mode (responder) never reaches that decision. |
| 0041 | `host/bluedroid/stack/btm/btm_sec.c` | `btm_io_capabilities_req()`: a pairing the device starts for a service (headphones mode authenticates the link it paged before AVDTP) answered the IO Capability Request with `BTM_AUTH_SP_NO`, i.e. **no bonding**; the peer may then drop the key at disconnect (BlueZ did, silicon 2026-11-25), and the next automatic reconnect needs a new pairing, which headphones mode refuses outside its pairing window. As initiator without dedicated bonding the reply now sets the general-bonding bit (`BTM_AUTH_GB_BIT`, MITM bit unchanged). Responder replies (phone mode) are unchanged. |

All patches are guarded with `#if defined(OPENFW_BLUEDROID) && OPENFW_BLUEDROID`; the `#else` branch is upstream.
Next free number on this branch: **0042**. Host coverage: `make -C open_fw test-bt-host` (Bluedroid on the FreeRTOS POSIX port,
`tests/bt_host/`) exercises 0005-0041 through the real `bt_ctrl` and the fake ROM (0024-0028 through the phone-mode
scenario `test_bt_host phone`: SSP, SDP, RFCOMM/SPP, XREC, teardown with a connected peer; 0040/0041 through
`test_bt_host_hp hps` S3, whose fake ROM models the single ext-features slot and the initiator pairing decision). The allocation-failure sweep runs
once per lifecycle call (`run_sweep.py --mode init|enable|disable|deinit`): every allocation attempt the call makes is
failed in turn, and each point must complete or fail cleanly, tear down to the heap/task/timer baseline and leave a
following clean cycle working, with **no waivers** (2026-11-24, after 0011-0023). Each of 0011-0023 was verified by
reverse-applying it alone on a scratch copy: the sweep of its mode then fails (`tests/bt_host/README.md`). 0008's RX
retry is covered by the same sweeps; 0009's restored slot is invisible to them (1 of 254 slots), so it has a direct
`fixed_queue` scenario (`test_bt_host fixedq`, capacity 2).

Failure semantics of 0011-0023 (one rule): an allocation failure inside a lifecycle call either **completes** the step
without the allocation (0014, 0015, 0017, 0018, 0023's osal table), **retries** a bounded number of ticks where the
event cannot be failed back to anyone (0016, 0019; then BT fault / upstream behaviour), or **fails the API call
cleanly** (0011-0013, 0020-0023): `esp_bluedroid_init()`/`enable()` return an error with the API state unchanged and
nothing left that blocks deinit + a later init/enable. After a failed `esp_bluedroid_enable()` the caller deinits
(the recovery ladder does); enable is not retried in place.
